messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 fired for region: eu-west-az3 — serving latency spike + 5xx surge detected across model shard pool. Alert group: az3-serving-degrade. Links: https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC-3421 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Automated page sent to @oncall (Maria Chen). Escalation policy: SRE-core -> SRE-leads at +5m if unacknowledged.
Maria Chen: ack'd via mobile. I'm coming online — grabbing runbook now. Can someone paste the quick status?
Jon Patel: seeing backend error rates from the runtime: KV cache thrash + GPU kernel queue length spiking. Logs: `runtime/serve: oom_backpressure=true, kv_evictions=high, tail_latency_ms=1200`
Kevin O'Leary: traffic jump ~3x in last 90s; autoscaler didn't spin up due to AZ capacity cap. Cloud has limited spare GPUs in eu-west-az3.
Maria Chen: OK, immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable fallback routing to eu-west-az2 (partial capacity) 2) throttle non-prod / low-priority customers 3) reduce batch window to 20ms to lower latency. Trying automation runbook now: `/runbook run az3-fallback`
ops-robot: runbook az3-fallback invoked by Maria Chen. Steps: verify failover eligibility -> run traffic-divert -> apply per-tenant rate limits.
Jon Patel: quick check: rolling reduce batch in runtime config (example):
```
PATCH /v1/configs/runtime
{ "batch_window_ms": 20, "max_batch_tokens": 512 }
```
Applying now to canary nodes.
pagerduty: Incident escalation timer paused (acknowledged). Next escalation at +5m if no progress.
Priya Rao: product impact check: which customers impacted? Any enterprise SLA hits?
Jon Patel: initial telemetry shows 18% of routed requests hitting 5xx, primarily for larger sequence workloads and chat sessions pinned to az3. A subset of enterprise customers on pinned Dedicated pools in az3 will see errors.
Maria Chen: notifying CS and Status page: drafting message — we'll state degraded performance in eu-west-az3, failover in progress, mitigation ETA ~12-20 minutes. @Priya can you review the wording?
Priya Rao: reviewing now. Suggest adding guidance: "retry after 30s" and note that embeddings/low-priority batch jobs may be throttled.
Kevin O'Leary: started traffic divert: `routerctl divert --from az3 --to az2 --percent 60`
ops-robot: divert command executed. Current split: az3=40% az2=60%. Monitoring propagation.
Jon Patel: canary nodes show drop in tail latency from 1200ms -> 420ms after batch change, 5xx rate down to 6% on canary. Good signal.
Maria Chen: good. Now applying per-tenant throttles for top 10 noisy customers in az3. Commands:
```
POST /v1/admin/throttle
{ "tenant_ids": [...], "qps": 5 }
```
Applying.
pagerduty: Automated escalation check: no change needed (ack still active).
Priya Rao: CS draft finalized and posted to status.redwood.io: "Degraded performance and increased errors in eu-west-az3. Traffic is being diverted to eu-west-az2. Some customers on pinned Dedicated pools may experience intermittent errors. We expect mitigation within ~20 minutes."
Maria Chen: note: autoscaler quota bump request submitted to cloud but will take 10-15m if approved; not counting on it for immediate fix.
Kevin O'Leary: started a manual hot-redeploy of a subset of serving instances (smaller memory config) to free up more slots: `deployctl redeploy --subset az3 --flavor compact`
Jon Patel: runtime notes: observed KV cache rehydrate spikes during divert. I've toggled `kv_cache_reclaim=false` temporarily to reduce churn. Watch for memory pressure.
Maria Chen: timeline update: divert at 60% completed. Errors trending down overall to ~3-4% cluster-wide. Still seeing error tail on long-seq workloads.
pagerduty: Alert: second policy trigger checked — no further escalation required.
Priya Rao: tagging Legal/Compliance because some customers are in regulated zones — any data plane changes?
Kevin O'Leary: no data plane modifications, only routing and config. All traffic stayed within eu-west region.
Maria Chen: incoming customer inquiry: "Are model outputs lost?" Answer: retries are safe; no permanent loss; some requests may have failed and should be retried.
Jon Patel: running short-term mitigation: enable degradation mode for non-interactive pipelines (disable deterministic sampling) to lower compute. Command: `runtimectl set-mode degrade-noninteractive true`
ops-robot: degradation mode enabled.
Maria Chen: status update for PD: mitigation engaged, traffic diverted, throttles in place, visible improvement. Next: monitor for 15m, then slowly return divert to 0% as AZ recovers.
Kevin O'Leary: cloud reports new capacity available in az3 (some preemptible GPUs freed). Starting controlled scale-up: `autoscaler attach --az az3 --units 4`
Jon Patel: after scale-up, I've seen KV cache warm and tail latency further reduce to ~180ms on recovered nodes. 5xx rate ~0.8% now.
Maria Chen: routing back: lowering divert to 30% -> 10% over next 10m.
Priya Rao: confirming customer comms: updated status with "Service performance improving; full recovery expected within 10-15 minutes. We will follow up with a post-incident summary."
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged -> resolving conditions met.
Maria Chen: closing notes: root cause initial: sudden traffic spike + AZ capacity quota + KV cache churn leading to backpressure. Remediation: traffic divert, per-tenant throttles, batch window reduce, temporary degradation mode, manual redeploys, autoscaler attach. Post-incident actions: 1) increase spare capacity buffer in az3 2) tune autoscaler to prefer faster scale decisions 3) KV cache reclaim safety net 4) improve runbook steps for quicker divert.
Jon Patel: saving logs and timeline to INC-3421 and creating a JIRA: SRE-987 for follow-ups.
Maria Chen: thanks team. Marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INC-3421 marked resolved by Maria Chen at ts=6201234700. Postmortem requested.
